import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Group by brand and calculate average megapixels and price
brand_avg = df.groupby('brand')[['megapixels', 'price_usd']].mean().reset_index()

# Create a bar plot to compare average megapixels and price across different brands
sns.set_style('whitegrid')
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.barplot(x='brand', y='megapixels', hue='brand', data=brand_avg, palette='Blues')
plt.title('Average Megapixels Across Different Brands')
plt.xlabel('Brand')
plt.ylabel('Average Megapixels')
plt.legend(title='Brand')
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a histogram to show the distribution of prices
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.histplot(df['price_usd'], bins=20, kde=True)
plt.title('Distribution of Prices')
plt.xlabel('Price (USD)')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output_prices.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a scatter plot to show the relationship between megapixels and price
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(x='megapixels', y='price_usd', data=df)
plt.title('Relationship Between Megapixels and Price')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels')
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)')
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output_megapixels_price.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
